Viernes 13 de noviembre de 2026  ·  796 palabras  ·  4 min de lectura

Nebuly protagoniza la apertura con un movimiento de capital que confirma el apetito inversor por la transformación del seguro. La jornada se completa con Matos Warns, que pone el foco en otro frente del mercado: el de cambio de liderazgo. De los 76 artículos rastreados hoy, 26 han activado nuestras alertas de señal — una densidad de noticias relevante que no veíamos en días. A continuación, las cinco historias que hemos seleccionado entre 76 artículos de más de 40 fuentes, ordenadas por impacto real sobre el negocio asegurador.

1. 💰 Inversión

Nebuly raises $21 million to measure AI returns

AI analytics startup Nebuly raised a $21 million Series A led by Planven, with participation from Exor Ventures, Tenacity Capital, TGVG Capital, Fastweb+Vodafone via Founders Factory, and returning investors and angels. Based in Turin and New York, Nebuly helps companies measure the business value of AI assistants used by employees and customers. Nebuly connects to existing AI tools, including custom agents and assistants based on Claude, ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot, and can run on-premises or in a customer’s private cloud.

  1. El dato clave: Nebuly raises $21 million to measure AI returns.
  2. La operación: $21M (Series A), una de las mayores transacciones detectadas en el sector en las últimas semanas.
  3. ¿Qué vigilar? El capital invertido anticipa las áreas donde los incumbentes afrontarán mayor presión competitiva en los próximos 12-24 meses.

2. 👔 Cambio de Liderazgo

ANZ CEO Matos Warns of Global Jobs Crisis Without AI Rules

Chief Executive Officer Nuno Matos has called for global regulation to manage the impact of artificial intelligence on the labor market, which he warned could trigger an international crisis. Should large-scale job cuts of up to 50% emerge, “we’ll have a crisis and it’s not going to be in Australia, it’s going to be a global crisis,” Matos said Thursday during a parliamentary hearing in Canberra. “I hope that obviously the world and the administrations are capable of cooperating and ensuring that this technology does not create a social problem at a global level,” Matos said.

  1. El dato clave: Should large-scale job cuts of up to 50% emerge, “we’ll have a crisis and it’s not going to be in Australia, it’s going to be a global crisis,” Matos said Thursday during a parliamentary hearing in Ca.
  2. ¿Por qué importa? Los cambios de liderazgo suelen anticipar cambios estratégicos.
  3. ¿Qué vigilar? Seguimiento recomendado desde las perspectivas de riesgo técnico, regulatorio y competitivo.

Pinion receives approval to acquire Catlin Specialty

Pinion US Holdings has received change-of-control approval from the Oklahoma Department of Insurance to complete its acquisition of Catlin Specialty Insurance Company, a US excess and surplus lines insurer. Pinion launched in February 2026 with a commitment of up to $180 million from asset manager Barings.

5. 💰 Inversión

VIG Re secures debut €60m Charles Bridge Re catastrophe bond priced at low-end

VIG Re, the reinsurance arm of Vienna Insurance Group, has now successfully priced its debut catastrophe bond, securing an upsized €60 million of fully-collateralized European windstorm retrocession from the Charles Bridge Re 2026 DAC issuance with the spread finalised at the low-end of reduced price guidance, Artemis understands. VIG Re entered the catastrophe bond market for the first time in October, initially seeking €50 million of retrocessional reinsurance windstorm protection from investors with this debut Charles Bridge Re deal. That low-end is now where the €60 million of Charles Bridge Re 2026 DAC Class A catastrophe bond notes have been priced, securing the protection from the capital markets for VIG Re, we are told.

  1. El contexto: VIG Re entered the catastrophe bond market for the first time in October, initially seeking €50 million of retrocessional reinsurance windstorm protection from investors with this debut Charles Bridge.
  2. ¿Por qué importa? Nueva financiación que puede acelerar la competencia en el sector.
  3. ¿Qué vigilar? El capital invertido anticipa las áreas donde los incumbentes afrontarán mayor presión competitiva en los próximos 12-24 meses.

Cortina: Just a soft market trend, or clearing the floor for reinsurance’s next act?

Cortina has raised a lot of questions in the market, as to whether the recently launched Aon structured and Blackstone backed reinsurance facility at Lloyd’s is simply the latest iteration of a soft market trend and evolution of following, tracker style capacity, or something more portending of future market developments. Apply that to reinsurance and the Lloyd’s market and Cortina becomes a signal of something potentially more meaningful and perhaps ominous, than just an extension of Aon’s Client Treaty with a single backer. A Cortina is a specific tango-related phrase, a brief musical interlude within the Argentine milonga (a social tango event), used to signal the end of one dance, the clearing of the floor for a new set of dancers, and it often signals a structural change to the rhythm that has been played.

Aviva Flags Higher UK Home Subsidence Claims After Dry Summer

Aviva Plc has seen higher UK subsidence claims, the latest sign of the impact of this summer’s heat wave, which has dried out soil and caused the ground beneath homes to sink or shift. The British insurer experienced a “peak subsidence period” in the third quarter and saw claims continue into October, Chief Executive Officer Amanda Blanc said in a phone interview after Aviva released its third-quarter trading update on Friday. Insurance claims tied to subsidence — a phenomenon associated with bouts of hot, dry weather that shrink the soil and destabilize the foundations on which buildings stand — hit a record earlier this year, according to the Association of British Insurers.

Weather disaster losses account for higher share of national income in 13 countries, Munich Re finds

Munich Re research published to coincide with COP 31 in Türkiye has found that weather-related disaster losses accounted for a higher average share of national income in 13 of the 20 countries studied over the past decade than in the first decade of the analysis. The global reinsurer compared losses from weather-related disasters, including floods, storms, hail and wildfires, with gross national income (GNI) in 20 selected countries over 40 years, from 1986 to 2025. Across the 20 countries combined, the share of recorded weather disaster losses that went uninsured fell from roughly two-thirds in 1986-1990 to half in 2021-2025 on average.

Some 40% of US Planned Data Center Capacity Is in States Wanting to Hit Pause

All told, about 40% of pending data center capacity in the US is planned to be built in states where newly elected governors have promised to stop or pause such construction, according to data from Cleanview, a market intelligence company. Newly elected governors in Ohio, Georgia, Michigan, New Mexico and Texas campaigned on a promise to stop — or at least pause — data center construction statewide, while those in New York and Oregon pledged to prolong pauses already in place. Democrats now control key branches of state government in some of the country’s data center hotbeds, including Virginia, Pennsylvania and Arizona, and are likely to pursue utility and permitting policies that stall construction, according to a new report from BloombergNEF.

A catastrophic 2025 Los Angeles firestorm exposed some 7 million people to high levels of airborne lead and other toxic metals released from burning homes and vehicles, according to a new study. Scientists for the first time were able to quantify in real time the chemical composition of wildfire smoke thanks to a sensor network that went online months before the January 2025 Eaton conflagration that destroyed more than 9,400 buildings, killing 19 people. Property cat rate declines to slow at Jan 1, supply of capital now much more disciplined: RenRe CUO

Global reinsurer RenaissanceRe (RenRe) expects property catastrophe rate declines to decelerate at the January 1 renewals, and also anticipates the market will remain disciplined with respect to terms and conditions and structures, noting that the supply of capital willing to accept risk is much more disciplined than it was a decade ago. So, the supply of capital willing to accept risk has been much more disciplined than what we might have seen 10 years ago, where flexibility of structures was more of the key,” explained Marra. In his prepared remarks, Marra said that ahead of the key January 1 renewals, RenRe expects the property market to remain competitive but attractive, with healthy demand likely to be outstripped by supply.

DOJ Recovers $604K in Back Wages from Indiana Auto Parts Manufacturer

Department of Labor has recovered $604,000 in back wages for 829 workers after an investigation found an Indianapolis-area vehicle parts manufacturer failed to properly calculate overtime wages. Toa (USA) LLC, with manufacturing facilities in Mooresville, is the primary body structure and suspension components supplier for Subaru of Indiana Automotive and Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing North America. Investigators with the department’s Wage and Hour Division found that Toa (USA) LLC, a major automotive supplier that serves top-tier automotive companies, did not include a non-discretionary attendance bonus for hourly employees when calculating overtime during applicable workweeks, in violation of the overtime provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act.
